newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB seeks Canadian government help to move grain.
newsitem.headline: CWB seeks Canadian government help to move grain.

text.p: The Canadian Wheat Board on Tuesday asked Canada's federal government to intervene in a "disastrous" situation where delayed rail shipment of grain has lead to more than 34 ships waiting to load on the Pacific.
The CWB estimated demurrage fees on those waiting vessels could be as high as C$15 million in the 1996/97 (Aug/July) crop year, a CWB release stated.
Any deficit incurred by the CWB is covered by Canadian taxpayers because the federal government guarantees farmers a minimum price at the outset of each crop year.
Exports through the Pacific are at a 10-year low, it said.
"This is in spite of the fact there is a full complement of rail cars, abundant grain stocks at country elevators and ample space at port elevators," the CWB statement said.
Western Canadian farmers harvested a record crop of the six major grains and oilseeds this fall, CWB and Statistics Canada figures show.
"Adverse weather conditions have been a factor, but cannot account for the huge shortfall in rail car unloads," it added.
Although farmers are guaranteed a minimum price, the CWB estimated the delayed movement of grain could cost farmers at least C$65 million in lost revenue and demurrage fees.
"This will result in a direct loss of approximately C$50 million in revenue to the 1996/97 pool accounts," it added.
Canada's reputation as a reliable supplier is also at risk, the CWB said.
"Customers have some sympathy for weather or labour-related problems, but they cannot be expected to understand this obvious lack of performance," the CWB's Hehn said.
The CWB did not elaborate in what ways, specifically, the government might be able to alleviate the situation.
